title: Externally-owned worktrees
description: HAR runs inside checkouts it did not create — an external orchestrator's worktree, or the main checkout itself. Each station adds a question the gate keeps asking forever: does HAR know it does not own the checkout, does evidence written there reach Mission Control and the portal, and does teardown leave the orchestrator's workspace alone.

stations.title: HAR knows it does not own the checkout
stations.description: `--no-worktree` no longer collapses the main checkout and a foreign worktree into one mode. Detection is git-based, so any tool that creates a worktree (Warp, Conductor, cursor, a hand-rolled `git worktree add`) is covered without HAR knowing its name.

stations.title: Evidence written there reaches Mission Control and the portal
stations.description: Repository identity stays canonical — one row per repo, not one per worktree — while runs, work units, attempts, validations and bindings are read from the union of the canonical checkout and the workspace sync ran in. A source new to a watermark is sent unfiltered once.

stations.title: Teardown leaves a checkout HAR did not create alone
stations.description: An externally-created worktree is a real linked worktree, so `git worktree remove` would succeed on it. HAR removes only what HAR created; root mode no longer acts on its legacy guessed path either.

stations.title: A real external worktree, end to end — and the owned path unchanged
stations.description: Drives the built CLI through launch/verify/status/teardown inside a worktree created outside HAR, then does the same for a HAR-owned slot to prove the ordinary path did not regress.

handoff.waitFor: human review of the S3 lab report before merge
